issues.legal_issue: A statutory right to recover tax arrears from compensation does not require acceptance of compensation bonds already delivered to the intermediary.
material_facts: The respondent had unpaid agricultural income-tax and penalty arrears arising from an earlier period.
The respondent submitted compensation bonds to the tax authorities and asked that they be accepted towards the arrears.
The bonds had already been delivered to the respondent as payment of compensation.
The assessing officer and the Collector refused to accept the bonds.
issues.conclusion: The authorities were not required to accept the bonds in payment of the tax arrears, and the Collector was not in error by refusing them.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(d) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, and Rule 8A provide for recovery of specified arrears from compensation but do not require or authorize payment of tax by accepting compensation bonds. Collector of Sultanpur v. Raja Jagdish Prasad Sahi held that section 6(d) applies to the relevant agricultural income-tax arrears and that Rule 8A is mandatory; neither holding makes bonds a means of paying those arrears. Section 68 permits compensation to be paid in cash or bonds, and payment by bonds satisfies the compensation claim.

rule.if: tax_collection_proceeding and prevesting_tax_arrears and taxpayer_offered_bonds and compensation_already_paid_by_bonds

predicates.tax_collection_proceeding: A tax authority is seeking to collect unpaid tax from a taxpayer.
predicates.prevesting_tax_arrears: The unpaid tax arose for a period before the relevant property vested in the government.
predicates.taxpayer_offered_bonds: The taxpayer submitted bonds to the tax authority and asked that they be applied to the tax debt.
predicates.compensation_already_paid_by_bonds: The government had delivered bonds to the taxpayer as payment of compensation.

issues.definition: When a tax authority is collecting pre-vesting tax arrears, the taxpayer offers bonds, and compensation has already been paid in bonds, the authority is not required to accept those bonds for the tax.

issues.legal_issue: Delivery of compensation bonds satisfies the government's obligation to pay compensation, so the compensation does not remain payable until the bonds are encashed.
material_facts: The compensation bonds had been delivered to the respondent as payment of compensation for his former rights.
The bonds were payable in instalments and could not be cashed before their due dates.
issues.conclusion: The compensation claim was satisfied upon delivery of the bonds and did not continue to be payable until they were encashed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 68 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, provides for compensation to be paid in cash, bonds, or partly in each. The rules governing the bonds provide for payment of principal and interest in instalments and permit earlier redemption at the government's option. Delivery of bonds under that arrangement constitutes payment of compensation.

predicates.compensation_payment_proceeding: The government is paying compensation to a person whose rights have been acquired or extinguished.
predicates.government_delivered_bonds_as_compensati: The government delivered bonds to the person as payment of that compensation.

issues.definition: When the government delivers bonds as compensation, its compensation obligation is satisfied.

issues.legal_issue: The negotiability of compensation bonds does not make them legal tender or require a creditor, including the government, to accept them for a debt.
material_facts: The respondent argued that the bonds were negotiable and therefore had to be accepted for his tax debt.
The bonds were not cashable at the time he offered them.
issues.conclusion: The bonds' negotiability did not oblige the government to accept them in payment of the tax arrears.
issues.legal_principle: Negotiability allows the owner to transfer an instrument to a person willing to purchase it; it does not make the instrument legal tender or impose a duty on anyone, including the government, to accept it for payment of a debt.

predicates.payment_tender_dispute: A debtor offers an instrument to a creditor as payment of a debt.
predicates.negotiable_bonds_offered: The instrument offered is a bond that can be transferred by its owner.

issues.definition: When a debtor offers transferable bonds as payment, their transferability alone does not require the creditor to accept them.
